app.name: app-blueprint
app.summary: The repository's own plan: who builds which file of app-blueprint 2.0, taken from section 11 of the contract.

approach.layout: app-blueprint/ is the skill (SKILL.md, scripts, tests, references, assets); maintainers/ holds the maintainers' tools and the design contract; examples/ is generated; .blueprint/ is this plan.
approach.notes: A plan of files and owners only. Owner rules give every file, including files later waves will create, exactly one owner; maintainers/check_owned.py reads them to check a branch. Update the rules only when section 11 of maintainers/design/v2-contract.md changes.

decisions.decision: Files marked with a dagger in section 11 are recorded as W0-A2's; bp/version.py and the launcher (whole files), CHANGELOG.md, examples/**, .gitignore and the contract as orchestrator.
decisions.why: Section 11 hands the dagger files from W0-A1 to W0-A2 and the version lines, changelog and examples to the orchestrator after W0-A1 merges.

decisions.decision: Files no workstream of the table touches belong to the roster id maintainers.
decisions.why: Every tracked file needs exactly one owner; these are the pre-2.0 files that stay as they are.

decisions.decision: The .blueprint/** files are recorded as orchestrator, the final owner once the W0-C pull request merges (a third handover). maintainers/check_owned.py and its test stay W0-C.
decisions.why: Only a person or the orchestrator changes the plan; the check reads it from the base, so a builder branch cannot widen its own area.

decisions.decision: The tool copy in .blueprint/bin is not committed.
decisions.why: The repository is the tool; a copy would go stale at every version bump.

decisions.decision: The files of the finished W0-A1 workstream pass to W0-A2, which maintains the core.
decisions.why: W0-A1 is merged and closed; later core fixes touch its files and must pass the ownership check.
